text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.7% today as oil prices climbed sharply, with US crude hitting $103.37 per barrel—up notably from recent lows. The jump comes amid escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East: tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has remained resilient despite Iranian attacks, but negotiations between Qatari mediators and Tehran suggest potential for a broader U.S.-Iran deal that could ease regional risk premiums currently baked into crude prices. Higher oil prices directly lift the revenue and profits of crude producers like ConocoPhillips.

The two-week gain of 5.1% fits into a broader pattern where energy stocks have benefited from fuel supply tightness and elevated refining profits—the opposite of what President Trump promised voters on energy costs. Even as political pressure mounts on oil companies over high prices, the underlying fundamentals of tight supply and geopolitical uncertainty continue to support crude valuations and producer stock prices.
